_provenance: Federal (national) figures transcribed from IRS Rev. Proc. 2024-40 for Tax Year 2025 (single-filer schedule) and IRS Tax Topic 409 / the standard LTCG rate table. This pack models NATIONAL-LEVEL federal rules only; US state income tax and foreign tax credits are out of scope for v1 (docs/05-jurisdiction-tax-framework.md §5.7). Every value is a direct transcription of a published statutory figure so a reviewer can re-verify against the IRS source without re-deriving anything. Note that the engine's capitalGains.longTerm and incomeTax SLAB blocks model a single marginal rate (a deliberate simplification); the full progressive tables are recorded in the notes below and in the bracket arrays where the schema supports them.

incomeTax.note: Federal ordinary-income brackets for 2025 single filers (IRS Rev. Proc. 2024-40), as taxable income: 10% up to $11,925; 12% to $48,475; 22% to $103,350; 24% to $197,300; 32% to $250,525; 35% to $626,350; 37% above. The top bracket's 'upTo' uses a large finite sentinel since the schema requires a number. The engine prices retirement-year drawdown via marginalRateAtRetirement (a single planning assumption), not the full table; the table is recorded here for reference.

capitalGains.note: 2025 long-term capital gains are taxed at 0%/15%/20% by taxable income (single: 0% up to $48,350, 15% to $533,400, 20% above). The engine models a single marginal LTCG rate; this pack uses 15% as the most common planning assumption, with annualExemption 0 (US has no LTCG annual exemption). Short-term gains (held one year or less) are taxed as ordinary income. A 3.8% Net Investment Income Tax may add on top for high earners but is not modeled at national level in v1.

yieldIncome.note: Qualified dividends are taxed at long-term capital-gains rates (0/15/20%); ordinary dividends and interest are taxed as ordinary income. The engine keeps yield income structurally separate from capital gains; treatments below record the federal default.

withdrawalWaterfall.note: Taxable accounts (cash, CDs, brokerage, direct stocks) are drawn before tax-deferred retirement accounts (401(k)/IRA), which are taxed at ordinary income on withdrawal — mirroring the common tax-efficient US drawdown convention.
